policy_title: Deliver New Gigawatt Power Plant at Wylfa
stated: The Conservative Party will deliver a new gigawatt power plant at Wylfa in North Wales and work with industry to deliver existing projects at Hinkley Point and Sizewell.

source.quote: Deliver a new gigawatt power plant at Wylfa in North Wales and work with industry to deliver existing projects at Hinkley Point and Sizewell.

bearing_set.reason: Adding multi-gigawatt nuclear generation directly affects the UK's low-carbon electricity mix and emissions trajectory.
Nuclear baseload capacity can reduce energy price volatility and long-run electricity bills for households.
Domestic baseload nuclear generation reduces reliance on imported gas/LNG, concretely improving resilience to external energy-supply threats — a named O5 indicator.

Gigawatt-scale nuclear infrastructure materially affects long-run energy security, grid reliability and productive investment, all of which are genuine O13 indicators; the near-term cost (capital spend, construction) and long-term gain (stable cheap baseload, supply-chain development) diverge on the dual horizon.

Nuclear projects at this scale historically require substantial government financing guarantees or contracts-for-difference backstops (Wylfa/Hitachi collapsed partly for want of ~£20bn state backing); committing public credit or contingent liabilities of that magnitude materially moves the funded/borrowed balance indicator.

membership_note: Four genuine bearings: the policy's core decarbonisation effect (O6), its consumer energy-cost mechanism (O2), its aggregate prosperity and energy-security effect (O13), and its likely requirement for significant public financial commitment (O12). Employment effects are real but subsumed within O13 at this level of specificity.
